problems: The blind guess (a stick-figure human with outstretched limbs) does not match. The figure reads as a thin, bent diagonal line, not a recognisable spindle, so the subject is not identifiable from the silhouette.
The whorl (star 80331, at about x=231, y=274) is only a bright node with a small blue loop around it. It does not read as a weighted disc, which is the defining feature of a drop spindle.

The shaft kinks. The segment from hook 83895 (127,168) to whorl 80331 runs at roughly 45 degrees, but the segment from whorl 80331 to point 78180 (315,427) runs at roughly 60 degrees, with a bend at lower-shaft star 78527 (296,341). A spindle shaft should be a single straight line through the whorl.
The middle-of-shaft star 81660 (190,203) sits on a small bend in the upper shaft rather than on a clearly defined middle, so the upper shaft and middle are not distinct.

The trailing yarn is drawn as a spur from the whorl up-right to spun-yarn star 77277 (329,245), then down-right to end star 75458 (403,317). It is a zigzag, not a trailing thread, so the yarn does not read as spun yarn leaving the whorl.

Labels are clipped or overlap the figure: 'whorl, the weighted disc at the centre of the spindle' runs over the whorl and the blue outline, and 'point at the bottom of the spindle' is cut to 'point at the bottom of the s'.
The gold line sits almost exactly on the blue outline, so the figure is essentially a copy of the gold path rather than an independent silhouette.
output.advice:
